To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the moss Physcomittrella patens uses two different pathways to regulate electron flow in the thylakoid membrane: cyclic and pseudo-cycled electron flow.

the moss Physcomittrella patens uses two alternative pathways to regulate the photosynthetic electron flow, namely cyclic and pseudo-cyclical electron flow, and that the two pathways have a synergic effect in the regulation of the photosynthetic process.

both PGRL1 and FLV contribute to the regulation of photosynthesis in P. paten s, and that FLV activity is more relevant for the short-term regulation of photosynthesis whereas PGRL1 activity is more relevant in the long term.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the alternative electron flow processes in P. paten s.
the role of cyclic and pseudo cyclic electron transport in the regulation of light harvesting in the moss Physconitrella patens.
the role of cyclic and pseudo- cyclic electron transport in response of photosynthetic organisms to dynamic light conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PGRL1 and FLV pathways have a different role in photosynthetic regulation and photoprotection in moss.
the two alternative electron flow pathways are not interchangeable, but rather complementary, and that they are both essential for the regulation of photosynthesis in P. paten s.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both cyclic and pseudo-circular electron transport are involved in the regulation of electron transport and photoprotection in mosses.

the FLV-dependent pseudo-cyclic electron pathway is the first to react upon light change, whereas the PGRL1-dependent cyclic electron pathway is activated only after a longer period of strong illumination.
both cyclic and pseudo-circular electron flow contribute to the regulation of the photosynthetic electron flow in mosses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclic and pseudo cyclic electron flow are not mutually exclusive processes and both are important for the regulation of photosynthesis in response to dynamic illumination changes.

the regulation of photosynthesis is not only a matter of the relative abundance and activity of different electron transport pathways, but also of their temporal dynamics in response to dynamic changes in light intensity.
the moss P. paten is a suitable model to investigate the role of different alternative electron flow processes in response to dynamic changes in environmental conditions.
